A duplicate negative is made from a master positive, which in turn was made from an earlier negative. A duplicate is at least three generations from the original. Duplicate negatives may be prepared either to obtain characteristics not present in the original image, as in special effects work, or to protect and extend the production availability of the assembled original negative as when duplicate negatives are prepared for release printing simultaneously at different labs.

e.label: Master
e.description: Master that is usually positive and referred to as a master positive. It is a specially prepared positive print made from an earlier generation negative film and used for the preparation of duplicate negatives rather than for projection. The master is normally considered second generation material.

o.label: Original
o.description: Original that is usually negative. It is film exposed in a camera and thus of better quality than any subsequent generation or derivative. When referring to older film, an original is almost always a negative. However, the original film may also be a reversal positive.

r.label: Reference print/viewing copy
r.description: Reference print (ref print) that is defined technically as a release print which has been approved by the producer and director of a film. A reference print may also mean a print kept as a reference print to evaluate the quality of subsequent prints. In film archives, the term is used to indicate that a film may be viewed by researchers. It is not original, master, or duplicate material.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Generation stage of the film is not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

12.label: Base of film
12.description: Safety base film is a comparatively nonflammable film base that meets ISO requirements for a safety base. On some film, the phrase safety film appears on the edge of motion pictures. Nitrate film base is a highly flammable film base that does not meet the ISO requirements for safety base film.

a.label: Safety base, undetermined
a.description: Safety base film whose type has not been identified.

c.label: Safety base, acetate undetermined
c.description: Acetate safety base film whose exact type cannot be determined, i.e., where it is unknown if the type is diacetate or triacetate.

d.label: Safety base, diacetate
d.description: Cellulose diacetate film base. Introduced before World War I for home movies, diacetate base was more expensive and unpredictable than nitrate base and so failed to gain acceptance in professional 35 mm. film production.

i.label: Nitrate base
i.description: Cellulose nitrate film base. Cellulose nitrate support or base was used in the manufacture of 35 mm. film (and some 17.5 mm. film) until 1951. Nitrate base film is no longer manufactured.

m.label: Mixed base (nitrate and safety)
m.description: Combination of nitrate base and safety base film. The use of a mixed base was common in the early 1950s when nitrate base stock shots were spliced with safety base film for low-budget motion pictures. In such releases, up to 50% of the film consisted of stock shots on nitrate base film.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Item does not have a film base, e.g., paper film.

p.label: Safety base, polyester
p.description: Film base made of a synthetic resin (e.g., estar).

r.label: Safety base, mixed
r.description: Mixed safety base films spliced together, but no nitrate film.

t.label: Safety base, triacetate
t.description: Cellulose triacetate film base. Cellulose triacetate is a high acetal compound with very low flammability and slow burning characteristics. From 1951, triacetate has been used for professional as well as for amateur produced moving image film.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Base of the film is not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

13.label: Refined categories of color
13.description:
More specific color characteristics of the moving image than are contained in 007/03 (Color).

If the color portions of the item include more than one color process, a code for the predominant color process is given. The additional color processes are described in field 500 (General Note).

a.label: 3 layer color
a.description: Three layers of emulsion: cyan, magenta, and yellow. Each layer is sensitive to its own primary color. Beginning in the early 1950's, color film work has been done primarily on 3 layer, also called multilayer, film. This process is also known as integral tri-pack.

b.label: 2 color, single strip
b.description: Single strip of film was exposed with pairs of images by means of a beam-splitter prism. One of the pairs of images was exposed through a red filter and one through a green filter. The resulting negative was used to produce both prints consisting of two strips cemented together, and, later in the history of the process, two color dye transfer prints. Also known as red and green Technicolor, the process was used exclusively by Technicolor and had its heyday between 1922 and 1933, although it was used until 1936 for animated cartoons.

c.label: Undetermined 2 color
c.description: System of color reproduction, which cannot be specifically identified, in which the visible spectrum is divided either into blue and red regions or into green and red regions for recording and presentation. Although extensively used in early color film processes, the inherent inability of two components to reproduce a satisfactory range of hues rendered all such systems obsolete when three-color processes became readily available and relatively inexpensive.

d.label: Undetermined 3 color
d.description: System of color reproduction, which cannot be specifically identified, in which the visible spectrum is divided into three sections, normally red, green, and blue, for the purposes of recording and presentation.

e.label: 3 strip color
e.description: Color system in which three color-separation negatives were produced on black-and-white film. 3 strip color is often used synonymously with the trademark Technicolor. In the Technicolor three-component system, light reflected from the subject matter is transmitted through the single lens of a special camera where it strikes a prism. One part of the light is passed through the prism and a green filter to produce a green record. The remainder of the light is reflected from the prism and absorbed by negatives to produce red and blue records. Each of the negatives is developed to produce new negatives which resemble black-and-white negatives.

f.label: 2 strip color
f.description: Color system in which two strips of film, one to record red light and one to record blue, were run through the camera simultaneously and exposed through the base of the front piece of film. These two strips of negatives were then used to produce prints of duplitized film stock (film stock with emulsion on both sides of the base), with a red-dyed image on one side, and a blue-dyed or -toned image on the other. Although extensively used in early color film processes, the inherent inability of two components to reproduce the visible color spectrum rendered all such systems obsolete when three-color processes became readily available. The process used from about 1929 to about 1950 by, among others, the following companies: Cinecolor, Magnacolor, and Multicolor.

g.label: Red strip
g.description: Cinecolor process, in which the color separation record of blue-green light prints as red. In the Super Cinecolor process, the color separation record of green light which prints as magenta (called "red" by Cinecolor). In the two-color Technicolor process, the color separation record of green light which prints as red.

h.label: Blue or green strip
h.description: Cinecolor process and the Super Cinecolor process, in which the blue strip is the color separation record of red light which prints as blue-green (called "blue" by Cinecolor). In the two-color Technicolor process, the green strip is the color separation record of magenta-red light which prints as green.

i.label: Cyan strip
i.description: Color separation record of red light which prints as cyan.

j.label: Magenta strip
j.description: Color separation record of green light which prints as magenta.

k.label: Yellow strip
k.description: Color separation record of blue light which prints as yellow.

l.label: S E N 2
l.description: Successive exposure negative 2. S E N 2 is a method of motion picture color photography in which two color separation negative images were recorded on one strip of film by photographing each frame two times successively through red and blue filters. The resultant negative was subsequently optically printed by the use of a skip-frame mechanism. The process was restricted to the photography of animated cartoon and puppet subjects in which the movement from frame to frame could be controlled. The successive exposure process was rendered obsolete by the introduction of 3 layer (multilayer) color negative film.

m.label: S E N 3
m.description: Successive exposure negative 3. S E N 3 is a method of motion picture color photography in which three color separation negative images were recorded on one strip of film by photographing each frame three times successively through red, blue, and green filters. The resultant negative was subsequently optically printed by the use of a skip-frame mechanism. The process was usually restricted to the photography of animated cartoon and puppet subjects in which the movement from frame to frame could be controlled. The successive exposure process was rarely used after the introduction of 3 layer (multilayer) color negative film.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Item is not a color film.

p.label: Sepia tone
p.description: Sepia tone which is a conversion of a black-and-white image in silver to sepia (a brownish grey to dark olive brown) by metallic compounds. Sepia was the most common tone used, and was used in black-and-white prints of films for special sequences to enhance the dramatic or pictorial effect.

q.label: Other tone
q.description: Color created by chemically altering the color, for example, uranium produces red, or increasing the brilliance of a print. Toning differs from tinting in that the clear portions of the film remain unaffected. Only the silver image of the positive film becomes colored.

r.label: Tint
r.description: Early in the history of tinting, a tint was created by dipping film in a bath of chemical dyes to get a dominant hue. Later raw stock became available already tinted in eleven stock shades: peach blow, blue for moonlight, amber for firelight, etc. The tinting of a film may be in whole or in part. Tinting was common until the advent of sound.

s.label: Tinted and toned
s.description: Color has been added to a film by using a tinted base and a toned emulsion.

t.label: Stencil color
t.description: Color is added using stencils, one cut for each color. Stencil color replaced the hand-coloring used in earlier years.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Refined category of color is not known.

v.label: Hand colored
v.description: Image, produced by a photographic process, is hand colored. Used whenever code h (hand-colored) is present in 007/03 (Color).

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate, such as when no single color process is predominant.

14.label: Kind of color stock or print
14.description: Type of color film stock or color print the item represents.

a.label: Imbibition dye transfer prints
a.description: Film color prints created by the transfer of two or more differently colored dye images to a single strip of blank film. The dye transfer process was used only to produce prints. Imbibition dye transfer prints can be produced from film originally shot on either multi-strip or multi-layer film. The process was used only by the Technicolor Company from ca. 1928 to ca. 1975. The patents were sold to the People's Republic of China, and since ca. 1980, the process has been available only in China.

b.label: Three-layer stock
b.description: Color film stock with three layers of emulsion: cyan, magenta and yellow. Each layer is sensitive to its own primary color. Since the early 1950's, most color films have been both shot and printed on this stock. It is also called multilayer film stock.

c.label: Three layer stock, low fade
c.description: Color film stock with three layers of emulsion: cyan, magenta and yellow. Each layer is sensitive to its own primary color and stabilized to reduce color fading as much as possible. It has been available since ca. 1983.

d.label: Duplitized stock
d.description: Color print stock with emulsion on both sides. Usually one side is dyed red, and the other side is dyed or toned blue.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Item is not a color film.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Type of color film stock is not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

15.label: Deterioration stage
15.description:
Level of deterioration of the motion picture film.

Codes are listed according to the seriousness of the deterioration. If more than one condition is applicable to the film in hand, the code for the most serious condition is recorded.

a.label: None apparent
a.description: No deterioration is apparent on either nitrate or non-nitrate motion picture film.

b.label: Nitrate: suspicious odor
b.description: Codes b-h are used for recording nitrate deterioration. The codes are listed according to the seriousness of the condition of deterioration. If more than one condition is applicable to the film in hand, the code for the most serious condition is recorded.

k.label: Non-nitrate: detectable deterioration
k.description: Codes k-m are used to record deterioration of non-nitrate materials (safety film, etc.). The codes are listed according to the seriousness of the deterioration. If more than one condition is applicable to the film in hand, the code for the most serious condition is recorded.

16.label: Completeness
16.description: Whether or not the item being cataloged is judged to be complete.

c.label: Complete
c.description: Judged to be complete.

i.label: Incomplete
i.description: Judged to be incomplete.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Completeness is not applicable to the type of motion picture, e.g., home movies, unedited footage, outtakes, and in some cases, unidentified material, etc.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Completeness of the item is not known.

17-22.label: Film inspection date
17-22.description:
Six characters that indicate the most recent film inspection date; the date is recorded in the pattern ccyymm (century/year/month). A hyphen is used for any unknown portion of the date. Six fill characters (||||||) are used if no attempt is made to code these character positions.

Film inspection date may be the date the item was cataloged or the date it was viewed. If the date is completely unknown, six hyphens are recorded.

k.label: Nonprojected graphic
k.description: One-character alphabetic code indicates that the category of material to which the item belongs is nonprojected graphic which is generally a two-dimensional pictorial representation, often opaque (e.g., print, photoprint, drawing) or transparent, and not intended to be projected for viewing (e.g., a photographic negative). A fill character (|) is not allowed in this position.

01.label: Specific material designation
01.description: Special class of nonprojected graphic to which the item belongs, (e.g., a picture).

a.label: Activity card
a.description: A card printed with words, numerals, and/or pictures to be used by an individual or a group as a basis for performing a specific activity.

c.label: Collage
c.description: Original work created by affixing various materials (paper, wood, newspaper, cloth, etc.) to a surface.

d.label: Drawing
d.description: Original visual representation (other than a print or painting) made with pencil, pen, chalk, or other writing instrument usually on paper or similar nonrigid support.

e.label: Painting
e.description: Original visual representation produced by applying paint to a surface.

f.label: Photomechanical print
f.description: Any picture produced in imitation of another picture through the use of photographic process to transfer the image to a printing surface. Hence, a snapshot made to document a painting or a Xerox copy of a print are considered photomechanical reproductions. Art reproductions are included here.

g.label: Photonegative
g.description: Piece of film, a glass plate, or pattern on which a negative image appears, i.e., directly opposite to a positive image (photoprint), slide, or transparency, used to produce a positive print. Photonegatives do not include negative photoprints, photoprints that are a combination of negative and positive images, or photograms or solarized prints, all of which are considered to be techniques used when making photoprints.

h.label: Photoprint
h.description: Photoprints have a positive image made either directly or indirectly on a sensitized surface by the action of light or other radiant energy. The term photoprint rather than photograph is used here as a more precise term than photograph, which technically can cover both the print and the negative. Opaque stereographs are included here.

i.label: Picture
i.description:
Two-dimensional visual representation accessible to the naked eye and generally on an opaque backing.

Used when a more specific designation is unknown or not desired.

j.label: Print
j.description: Design or picture transferred from an engraved plate, wood block, lithographic stone, or other medium. Generally there are four types: planographic print, relief print, intaglio print, and stencil print.

l.label: Technical drawing
l.description: Cross section, detail, diagram, elevation, perspective, plan, working plan, etc., made for use in an engineering or other technical context.

n.label: Chart
n.description: Opaque sheet that exhibits data in graphic or tabular form, e.g., a wall chart.

o.label: Flash card
o.description: Card or other opaque material printed with words, numerals, or pictures and designed for rapid display.

r.label: Radiograph
r.description: A photograph produced by the passage of radiation, such as X rays, gamma rays, or neutrons, through an opaque object.

u.label: Unspecified
u.description: Special material designation for the nonprojected graphic is not specified.

z.label: Other
z.description:
None of the other codes is appropriate.

Includes mixed media productions made by a combination of free hand and printing techniques when one or the other does not predominate.

02.label: Undefined
02.description: Contains blank (#) or a fill character (|).

03.label: Color
03.description: Color characteristics of the nonprojected graphic.

a.label: One color
a.description:
Printed or executed in a single color. Used for monochrome art works. It is not used with photographic materials.

Does not include black.

b.label: Black-and-white
b.description: Printed or executed in black-and-white. Refers to monochrome photographic materials executed in black-and-white.

c.label: Multicolored
c.description: Printed or executed in more than one color. Used for color photographic processes.

h.label: Hand colored
h.description: Image, produced by a printing or photographic process, is hand colored. Rarely used with commercial visual materials since these are not typically issued with hand coloring.

m.label: Mixed
m.description: Work or collection is a combination of one color, black-and-white, multicolored, hand colored, and/or other images.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Color characteristics of the item are not known.

z.label: Other
z.description:
None of the other codes is appropriate.

Includes stained, tinted, or toned items(e.g., sepia toned photographic items).

04.label: Primary support material
04.description:
Type of material used for the support or base on which an image is printed or executed.

Intended for use in handling and storage of material.

b.label: Bristol board
b.description: Fine, smooth pasteboard used by artists and painters.

e.label: Synthetic
e.description: Man-made substances other than textiles, plastic, and vinyl.

f.label: Skin
f.description:
Excludes leather, parchment, and vellum.

Synthetic materials that are made to resemble animal skin are coded as synthetic.

g.label: Textile
g.description:
Includes all natural or synthetic fibre fabrics except canvas.

Synthetic materials formed to resemble a fabric are considered textiles.

m.label: Mixed collection
m.description:
Primary support material varies for different items in a collection.

Typically this would be used for groups of nonprojected graphics on various bases.

n.label: Vellum
n.description: Fine-grained unsplit lambskin, kidskin, or calfskin prepared especially for writing or drawing on.

o.label: Paper
o.description: Any kind of cellulose-based paper.

p.label: Plaster
p.description: Includes mixtures of ground solids and plaster.

r.label: Porcelain
r.description:
Used only for clay-based porcelain.

Porcelain-like synthetic materials are coded e.

t.label: Wood
t.description: Material that is based on wood particles or fibers may or may not be considered wood. Consider particle board wood.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Primary support material is not known.

v.label: Leather
v.description: Animal skin dressed for use.

w.label: Parchment
w.description: Skin of a sheep or goat prepared for writing on.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

05.label: Secondary support material
05.description:
Type of material (other than normal museum matting) to which the primary support (007/04) is attached.

Used only when the mount or mat is of historical, informational, aesthetic, or archival importance.

b.label: Bristol board
b.description: Fine, smooth pasteboard used by artists and painters.

e.label: Synthetic
e.description: Man-made substances other than textiles, plastic, and vinyl.

f.label: Skin
f.description:
Excludes leather, parchment, and vellum.

Synthetic materials that are made to resemble animal skin are coded as synthetic.

g.label: Textile
g.description: Includes all natural or synthetic fibre fabrics except canvas.

m.label: Mixed collection
m.description:
Secondary support material varies for different items in a collection.

Typically this would be used for groups of nonprojected graphics on various bases.

n.label: Vellum
n.description: Fine-grained unsplit lambskin, kidskin, or calfskin prepared especially for writing or drawing on.

o.label: Paper
o.description: Any kind of cellulose-based paper.

p.label: Plaster
p.description: Includes mixtures of ground solids and plaster.

r.label: Porcelain
r.description:
Used only for clay-based porcelain.

Porcelain-like synthetic materials are coded e.

t.label: Wood
t.description: Material that is based on wood particles or fibers may or may not be considered wood. Consider particle board wood.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Secondary support material is not known.

v.label: Leather
v.description: Animal skin dressed for use.

w.label: Parchment
w.description: Skin of a sheep or goat prepared for writing on or strong, tough, and often somewhat translucent paper made to resemble parchment.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

q.label: Notated music
q.description: One-character alphabetic code that indicates the category of material to which the item belongs is notated music, which is defined as graphic, non-realized representations of musical works, both in printed and digitized manifestations. It includes musical scores and/or parts, diagrammatic representations, tablature, instructions for chance compositions, pictures or paintings intended as musical compositions, square note notation, klavarskribo, chant notation, neumes, braille, and other ways of representing the four components of musical sound: pitch, duration, timbre, and loudness. Notated music is often the means for communicating to the performer(s) how the musical work notated therein is to be realized in sound. A fill character (|) is not allowed in this position.

01.label: Specific material designation
01.description: Special class of textual material to which an item belongs.

u.label: Unspecified
u.description: Special material designation for the notated music is not specified.

00.label: Category of material
00.description: One-character alphabetic code that indicates the category of material to which the item belongs is projected graphic which is defined as a two-dimensional representation intended to be projected without motion by means of an optical device, for example, a filmstrip, slide, or transparency. A fill character (|) is not allowed in this position.

01.label: Specific material designation
01.description: Special class of projected graphic to which the item belongs, e.g., a slide.

c.label: Filmstrip cartridge
c.description: Item is a filmstrip which is encased in a cartridge and which has the ends joined to form a loop. A cartridge denotes a permanently encased single reel of film or tape that has the ends joined together to form a loop that provides playback without rewinding.

d.label: Filmslip
d.description: Item is a short filmstrip not in a roll.

f.label: Filmstrip, type unspecified
f.description: Item is a filmstrip other than a filmstrip cartridge, filmslip, or filmstrip roll or is an unspecified type of filmstrip.

o.label: Filmstrip roll
o.description: Item is a filmstrip roll, a roll of film on which still images are recorded, presenting an integrated communication. It is intended for projection frame by frame.

s.label: Slide
s.description:
Slides are transparent material on which there is a two-dimensional image, usually held in a mount, and designed for use in a projector or viewer.

Includes modern stereographs, e.g., Viewmaster reels.

t.label: Transparency
t.description: Transparencies are made of transparent material on which an image is recorded. They are designed for use with a projector or a light box. X-rays are included here.

u.label: Unspecified
u.description: Special material designation for the projected graphic is unspecified.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

02.label: Undefined
02.description: Contains blank (#) or a fill character (|).

03.label: Color
03.description: Color characteristics of a projected graphic.

a.label: One color
a.description:
Image is printed or executed in a single color (i.e., monochromatic). In projected graphic materials, it is used only for transparency sets.

Does not include black.

b.label: Black-and-white
b.description:
Image is printed or executed in black-and-white. Refers to monochrome photographic materials (including film) and videorecordings, or to overhead transparencies executed in black-and-white.

Does not include tinted, toned, or stained items.

c.label: Multicolored
c.description: Image is printed or executed in more than one color. The color is a result of a number of processes, either photographic or electronic, capable of reproducing a reasonable range of hues, or of original application of color materials, for example, paint. Code c is used for color photographic processes (motion pictures, filmstrips, transparencies, and slides), color videorecordings, or multicolored overhead transparencies.

h.label: Hand colored
h.description: Image, produced by a printing or photographic process, is hand colored. Code h is rarely used with commercial audiovisual materials since these are not typically issued with hand coloring.

m.label: Mixed
m.description: Work or collection is a combination of one color, black and white, colored, hand colored, and/or other images. Information for this data element is based on one of the following phrases: some col., some b&w, 25 gold toned, col. with b&w sequences, etc. which usually appears in other parts of the MARC record.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Item has no images. Used, for example, when the item in hand is sound track film intended to accompany visual images not actually present.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Color characteristics of the projected graphic are not known.

z.label: Other
z.description:
None of the other codes is appropriate.

Includes tinted, toned (e.g., sepia toned photographic items), or stained items.

04.label: Base of emulsion
04.description: Type of material for the base of the emulsion of a photonegative, filmstrip, slide, or transparency.

d.label: Glass
d.description: Primary support/base of the emulsion material is glass.

e.label: Synthetic
e.description: Primary support/base of the emulsion material is synthetic (e.g., plastics, vinyl, etc.). Most commercially issued overhead transparency sets have a synthetic primary support material, unless known to be otherwise.

j.label: Safety film
j.description: Primary support/base of the emulsion material is safety (i.e., not nitrate) film. For all commercially issued filmstrips and slide sets, assume that the base of the emulsion is safety film unless known to be otherwise.

k.label: Film base, other than safety film
k.description: Primary support/base of the emulsion material is not safety film.

m.label: Mixed collection
m.description:
Primary support/base of the emulsion material varies for different items in a collection.

Typically this would be used for groups of projected graphics on various bases.

o.label: Paper
o.description: Primary base of the emulsion is any kind of cellulose-based paper.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Primary support/base of the emulsion material for the projected graphic is not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

05.label: Sound on medium or separate
05.description: Whether the sound is on or is separate from the projected graphic (i.e., on the accompanying material).

.label: No sound (silent)
.description: For filmstrips, slides, and transparencies, code # is used when there is no information about sound in subfield $b or $e of field 300. For kits containing any of the above items, the abbreviation si. or the fact that there is no statement pertaining to sound in field 500 (General Note) justifies use of code #.

a.label: Sound on medium
a.description: Sound is present and is on the item.

b.label: Sound separate from medium
b.description: Sound is on an accompanying item.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Presence of sound on the item is not known.

06.label: Medium for sound
06.description:
Specific medium used to carry the sound of an item (whether the sound is on the projected graphic or separate) and the type of sound playback required for the item.

Used in conjunction with the information coded in 007/05 (Sound on medium or separate) and 007/07 (Dimensions). Typically, the carriers of sound are: 1) optical and/or magnetic track on a film reel or encased in a cassette or cartridge; 2) audio or video tape which may be on a reel or encased in a cassette or cartridge; and 3) sound or video disc.

.label: No sound (silent)
.description: Sound is not present.

a.label: Optical sound track on motion picture film
a.description: Sound to accompany a projected graphic is carried on an optical track that is part of a film. In coding 16 and 35 mm. films, it is usually assumed that sound is carried on an optical track.

b.label: Magnetic sound track on motion picture film
b.description: Sound to accompany a projected graphic is carried on a magnetic track that is part of the film. 70 mm. motion picture films often include magnetic sound tracks.

c.label: Magnetic audio tape in cartridge
c.description: Sound to accompany an item is carried on a magnetic audio tape cartridge.

d.label: Sound disc
d.description: Sound to accompany an item is carried on a sound disc. This method of providing for sound is typically used with filmstrips. Sound discs include 7, 10, and 12 in. vinyl phonograph records (identified as analog sound discs in subfield $b of field 300) and 4 3/4 in. compact discs (identified as digital sound discs in subfield $b of field 300)

e.label: Magnetic audio tape on reel
e.description: Sound to accompany an item is carried on a reel of magnetic audio tape.

f.label: Magnetic audio tape in cassette
f.description: Sound to accompany an item is carried on a cassette of magnetic audio tape.

g.label: Optical and magnetic sound track on motion picture film
g.description: Sound to accompany a projected graphic is carried on both an optical and magnetic track.

h.label: Videotape
h.description: Sound to accompany an item is included as part of a videotape. Videotape is not ordinarily used to record only sound.

i.label: Videodisc
i.description: Sound to accompany an item is included as part of a videodisc. Videodiscs are not ordinarily used to record only sound. A distinction must be made between videodiscs (e.g., 12 in. laser-scan videodiscs that include video information) and compact discs that are used to record sound only (e.g., 4 3/4 in. audio compact discs). The technology to physically record video or audio information on digital disc systems is the same.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Medium for sound is not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

07.label: Dimensions
07.description:
Width or dimensions of the projected graphic item.

Width is given for filmstrips. Height and width are given for slides and transparencies. Only the most common dimensions are indicated. For film and slides, only codes that exactly match the measurements of the item as given in the physical description should be used. If no code exactly matches, code z is used. For transparencies, the code that most closely approximates the dimensions as stated in the physical description is used. The dimensions for slides and transparencies include the size of the mount for the item.

a.label: Standard 8 mm. film width
a.description: Width of the film is standard 8 mm. Film termed Mauer 8 mm. is recorded as code a.

b.label: Super 8 mm./single 8 mm. film width
b.description: Width of the film is super 8 mm. Single 8 mm. film is a Japanese equivalent of super 8 mm. film.

j.label: 2x2 in. or 5x5 cm. slide
j.description: Dimensions of the slide in its mounting are either 2x2 in. or 5x5 cm.

k.label: 2 1/4 x 2 1/4 in. or 6x6 cm. slide
k.description: Dimensions of the slide in its mounting are either 2 1/4 x 2 1/4 in. or 6x6 cm.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Dimensions are not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

08.label: Secondary support material
08.description: Type of material of the mount of a slide or transparency for a projected graphic.

.label: No secondary support
.description: Filmstrips are always coded #.

c.label: Cardboard
c.description: Cardboard mount. Slides and transparencies cataloged from data sheets are assumed to have cardboard mounts unless otherwise known.

d.label: Glass
d.description: Glass mount that usually covers the film base but should not be the primary support for the film emulsion.

e.label: Synthetic
e.description: Secondary support material is synthetic (e.g. plastics, vinyl, etc.).

h.label: Metal
h.description: Metal is usually used to frame larger projected graphics which need better support.

j.label: Metal and glass
j.description: Metal portion is usually a frame that holds one or two pieces of glass to support the film base. Glass should not be the primary support for the film emulsion.

k.label: Synthetic and glass
k.description: Synthetic material, e.g., plastics, vinyl, etc., is usually used as a frame to hold one or two pieces of glass to support the film base. Glass should not be the primary support for the film emulsion.

m.label: Mixed collection
m.description:
Secondary support material varies for different items in a collection.

Typically this is used for groups of projected graphics on various secondary support materials.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Secondary support material is not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

r.label: Remote-sensing image
r.description: One-character alphabetic code that indicates the category of material to which the item belongs is remote-sensing image which is defined as an image produced by a recording device that is not in physical or intimate contact with the object under study. This may be a map or other image that is obtained through various remote sensing devices such as cameras, computers, lasers, radio frequency receivers, radar systems, sonar, seismographs, gravimeters, magnetometers, and scintillation counters. When the image has cartographic or bibliographic information added, it is referred to as a remote-sensing map. A fill character (|) is not allowed in this position.

01.label: Specific material designation
01.description: Special class of material, usually the class of physical object, to which an item belongs..

u.label: Unspecified
u.description: Special material designation of the remote sensing image is not specified.

02.label: Undefined
02.description: Contains blank (#) or a fill character (|).

03.label: Altitude of sensor
03.description: General position of the sensor relative to to the object under study.

a.label: Surface
a.description: Remote-sensing image was made from a device located on the surface of a body, usually a planet or moon.

b.label: Airborne
b.description: Remote-sensing image was made from a device above the surface of a body, generally in the atmosphere, an aircraft, balloon, or some other airborne device.

c.label: Spaceborne
c.description: Remote-sensing image was made from a device in space. Spaceborne sensors are those located outside the primary layers of an atmosphere (usually in orbit) and beyond.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Altitude of the sensor is not applicable to the image.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Altitude of the sensor from which the image was made is not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

04.label: Attitude of sensor
04.description: General angle of the device from which the remote-sensing image is made.

a.label: Low oblique
a.description: Remote-sensing device is closer to parallel with the surface being imaged than perpendicular.

b.label: High oblique
b.description: Remote-sensing device is closer to perpendicular than not.

c.label: Vertical
c.description: Angle of the remote-sensing device is vertical to the surface being imaged.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Angle of the remote-sensing device is not applicable, generally, because the attitude does not affect the image.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Angle of the remote-sensing device is not known.

05.label: Cloud cover
05.description: Amount of cloud cover that was present when a remote-sensing image was made.

0.description: Cloud cover present when an image was taken was between 0 and 9%.

1.description: Cloud cover present when an image was taken was between 10 and 19%.

2.description: Cloud cover present when an image was taken was between 20 and 29%.

3.description: Cloud cover present when an image was taken was between 30 and 39%.

4.description: Cloud cover present when an image was taken was between 40 and 49%.

5.description: Cloud cover present when an image was taken was between 50 and 59%.

6.description: Cloud cover present when an image was taken was between 60 and 69%.

7.description: Cloud cover present when an image was taken was between 70 and 79%.

8.description: Cloud cover present when an image was taken was between 80 and 89%.

9.description: Cloud cover present when an image was taken was between 90 and 100%.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Cloud cover is not applicable to the image.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Amount of cloud cover is not known.

06.label: Platform construction type
06.description: Type of construction of the platform serving as the base for the remote-sensing device. For the purposes of this data element, "platform" refers to any structure that serves as a base, not only flat surfaces.

a.label: Balloon
a.description: Base for the remote-sensing device was a balloon or similar lighter-than-air platform.

b.label: Aircraft--low altitude
b.description: Base for the remote-sensing device was an dynamic lift aircraft designed for low altitude flight (below 29,500 ft. (8,962 m.)).

c.label: Aircraft--medium altitude
c.description: Base for the remote-sensing device was an dynamic lift aircraft designed for medium altitude flight (between 29,500 ft. (8,962 m.) and 49,000 ft. (14,810 m.)).

d.label: Aircraft--high altitude
d.description: Base for the remote-sensing device was an dynamic lift aircraft designed for high altitude flight (above 49,000 ft. (14,810 m.)).

e.label: Manned spacecraft
e.description: Base for the remote-sensing device was a manned spacecraft.

f.label: Unmanned spacecraft
f.description: Base for the remote-sensing device was an unmanned spacecraft.

g.label: Land-based remote-sensing device
g.description: Base for the remote-sensing device was a land-based.

h.label: Water surface-based remote-sensing device
h.description: Base for the remote-sensing device was designed to remain on the surface of a body of water (e.g., a ship or floating platform).

i.label: Submersible remote-sensing device
i.description: Base for the remote-sensing device was designed to be submerged beneath the surface of a body of water (e.g., a submersible vessel or platform).

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Construction type of the platform from which the remote-sensing image was made is not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

07.label: Platform use category
07.description: Primary use intended for the platform specified in 007/06 (Platform construction type).

a.label: Meteorological
a.description: Primary use for the platform is to make remote-sensing images of meteorological events and conditions.

b.label: Surface observing
b.description: Primary use for the platform is to make remote-sensing images of the surface of a planet, moon, etc. (including the Earth).

c.label: Space observing
c.description: Primary use for the platform is to make remote-sensing images of space.

m.label: Mixed uses
m.description: Platform from which remote-sensing images can be made is designed for a variety of uses (i.e., uses covered by two or more of the other codes).

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Identification of platform use category is not applicable.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Platform use category is not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

08.label: Sensor type
08.description: For the recording mode of the remote-sensing device, specifically, whether the sensor is involved in the creation of the transmission it eventually measures.

a.label: Active
a.description: Sensor measures the strength of reflections of its transmissions sent to a remote target.

b.label: Passive
b.description: Sensor measures the strength of transmissions (e.g., radiation) emitted by a remote target without stimulation by the sensor.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Involvement of remote-sensing device in the creation of the transmission it measured is not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

09-10.label: Data type
09-10.description:
Spectral, acoustic, or magnetic characteristics of the data received by the device producing the remote-sensing image. It can be used to indicate both the wave length of radiation measured and the type of sensor used to measure it.

Section provides guidelines for the application of some data type codes. Most of the other codes are self-explanatory.

mm.label: Combination of various data types
mm.description: More than one data type is applicable to the remote-sensing image.

nn.label: Not applicable
nn.description: Data type is not applicable to the remote-sensing image being described.

pa.label: Sonar--water depth
pa.description: Acoustical data type for the remote-sensing image for water depth is sonar. This code is also used for echo-sounding images.

pb.label: Sonar--bottom topography images, sidescan
pb.description: Acoustical data type for the remote-sensing image is sidescan imaging. Sidescan imaging includes both near-surface and near-bottom sensing data.

pc.label: Sonar--bottom topography, near-surface
pc.description: Acoustical data type for the remote-sensing image is near-surface.

pd.label: Sonar--bottom topography, near-bottom
pd.description: Acoustical data type for the remote-sensing image is near-bottom (i.e., taken from 10-150 m. (33-494 ft.) from the bottom).

uu.label: Unknown
uu.description: Data type for the remote-sensing image is not known.

zz.label: Other
zz.description: None of the other codes is appropriate (e.g., x-rays).

s.label: Sound recording
s.description: A storage medium containing recorded sound or a representation of a musical composition from which sound can be mechanically reproduced, such as a piano roll. A fill character (|) is not allowed in this position.

01.label: Specific material designation
01.description: Special class of sound recording to which the item belongs (e.g., a cylinder).

b.label: Belt
b.description: A loop of flexible plastic or magnetic film on which audio signals are mechanically recorded, commonly known under the trade name Dictabelt.

d.label: Sound disc
d.description: Sound discs are thin circular objects that vary in diameter (e.g., 7 in., 10 in., 12 in.), on which sound waves, recorded as modulations or pulses, are incised or indented. Compact audio discs are typically 4 3/4 in. in diameter.

e.label: Cylinder
e.description: Cylinders are cylindrical objects on which sound waves are incised or indented in a continuous circular groove. Mass-produced cylinders are made of plastic. Early cylinders were made of tinfoil or wax.

g.label: Sound cartridge
g.description: Sound cartridges are containers holding a single sound tape, run as an endless loop.

i.label: Sound-track film
i.description: Sound-track film is a sound recording on film that is not intended to accompany visual images. Note: Code i is also to be used when it is not known if a sound recording on film is intended to accompany visual images.

q.label: Roll
q.description: Roll of paper, for example, for player piano or player organ, on which the notes of a musical composition are represented by perforations in the paper and from which sound can be mechanically produced.

r.label: Remote
r.description: Digital sound recording that is accessed, processed, executed, etc. remotely. In this case, the digital sound recording is used via input/output devices connected electronically to a computer. Frequently this involves connection through a computer network.

s.label: Sound cassette
s.description: Sound cassette is a container holding a narrow, usually 1/8 inch, sound tape on two reels, one to feed (and rewind) and the other to take up the sound tape.

t.label: Sound-tape reel
t.description: Sound-tape reel is usually designated an Open Reel or Reel-to-Reel. It is an audiotape-transport system with separate supply (feed) and take-up reels.

u.label: Unspecified
u.description: Special material designation for the sound recording is not specified.

w.label: Wire recording
w.description: Wire recording is a round steel wire on which sound waves are magnetically recorded.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

02.label: Undefined
02.description: Contains blank (#) or a fill character (|).

03.label: Speed
03.description:
Playback speed of the sound recording. This code is only intended to relate to the playing speed of a sound recording rendered on a mechanical device.

Speed is associated with the kind of item with which it is associated; either disc (007/01 is code d), cylinder (007/01 is code e), or tape (007/01 is code g, s, or t.)

Codes a, b, c, d, e indicate that the rotational speed of a sound disc is equal to the value of revolutions per minute (RPM) represented by the specific code. Certain speeds are usually associated with the diameter of the disc (e.g., 10 in. discs are played back at 78 rpm, 7 in. discs are played back at 45 rpm, 12 in. discs are played back at 33 1/3 rpm). Playback speed is not absolutely associated with any one disc size.

f.label: 1.4 m. per second (discs)
f.description: Speed is calculated from the distance the playback mechanism covers on the surface of the disc per second, and not the number of revolutions of the disc. It is associated with compact discs (CDs).

k.label: 15/16 ips (tapes)
k.description: Speed occurs, for example, on half-speed mini-cassettes used in small portable recorders.

l.label: 1 7/8 ips (tapes)
l.description: Speed occurs, for example, on standard cassettes.

m.label: 3 3/4 ips (tapes)
m.description: Speed occurs, for example, on consumer and nonprofessional reel-to-reel tapes, cartridges and very unusual cassette tapes.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Speed is not applicable to remote digital sound recordings because it pertains to calculations specific to physical aspects of carriers.

o.label: 7 1/2 ips (tapes)
o.description: Speed occurs, for example, in reel-to-reel, nonprofessional, and studio tapes.

p.label: 15 ips (tapes)
p.description: Speed occurs, for example, on reel-to-reel, studio tapes.

r.label: 30 ips (tape)
r.description: Speed occurs, for example, on reel-to-reel, studio tapes, but is rarely used.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

04.label: Configuration of playback channels
04.description:
Configuration of playback channels for a sound recording.

Monaural, stereophonic, quadraphonic, and other configuration of playback channels should be coded based on a clear indication of intended playback. These codes do not refer to the configuration of channels orginally recorded, unless those channels are all intended to be available on playback.

m.label: Monaural
m.description: Configured to be played back on one channel.

q.label: Quadraphonic, multichannel, or surround
q.description: Configured to be played back on more than two channels. Use this code for Dolby surround sound tracks and other multichannel techniques.

s.label: Stereophonic
s.description: Configured to be played back on two separate channels.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Configuration of playback channels is not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

05.label: Groove width/groove pitch
05.description: Width of the groove of the recording for discs or the pitch of the groove for cylinders.

m.label: Microgroove/fine
m.description: Microgroove disc or a fine cylinder. Discs issued at 16, 33 1/3, and 45 rpm are usually issued as microgroove. Cylinders issued at 160 rpm (which have 200 grooves per inch) are usually issued as fine.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Item does not contain grooves. Used for tapes and compact audio discs.

s.label: Coarse/standard
s.description: Coarse or standard groove. Discs issued at 78 rpm are usually coarse. Cylinders issued at 120 rpm (which have 100 grooves per inch) are usually standard.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Groove width/groove pitch is not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

06.label: Dimensions
06.description: Diameter of an open reel or disc, or the dimensions of a cassette, cartridge, or cylinder.

j.label: 3 7/8 x 2 1/2 in.
j.description: Height and width of the cassette are 3 7/8 x 2 1/2 in. Used for a standard compact cassette.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Sound recording is not a reel, disc, cassette, cartridge, or cylinder.

o.label: 5 1/4 x 3 7/8 in.
o.description: Height and width of the cartridge are 5 1/4 x 3 7/8 in. Used for a standard audio cartridge.

s.label: 2 3/4 x 4 in.
s.description: Dimensions of a cylinder are 2 3/4 in. (diameter) x 4 in. (length).

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Dimensions of the sound recording are not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

07.label: Tape width
07.description:
Width of the tape.

Cassette implies code l, cartridge implies code m, and tape reel implies code m.

l.label: 1/8 in.
l.description: Most cassettes use 1/8 in. tape.

m.label: 1/4 in.
m.description: Nonprofessional, consumer, and some professional reels, and most 8-track cartridges use 1/4 in. tape.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Item is not a tape or does not include a tape. For example, code n is used if the item is a disc.

o.label: 1/2 in.
o.description: Recording studios customarily use 1/2 in. tape. Some 8-track cartridges have been issued in 1/2 in. tape.

p.label: 1 in.
p.description: Recording studios often use 1 inch tape. Some 8-track cartridges have been issued in 1 in. tape.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Tape width is not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

08.label: Tape Configuration
08.description:
Number of tracks on a tape.

Cassette implies code c; cartridge implies code d. There is no standard number of tracks for tape reels.

a.label: Full (1) track
a.description: Full or single track.

b.label: Half (2) track
b.description: Half track configuration is used to permit two tracks (channels) to be recorded on one tape. It is used with audio cassettes to permit monoaural recordings in two directions and with stereophonic recordings in one direction.

c.label: Quarter (4) track
c.description: Quarter track configuration is used to permit four tracks (channels) to be recorded on one tape. It is used with standard audio cassettes to permit stereophonic recordings in two directions, and with quadraphonic recordings in one direction.

d.label: Eight track
d.description: Eight track configuration is used with monaural, stereophonic, and quadraphonic recordings. Commercial eight track cartridges customarily include four pairs of stereophonic (two track) recordings.

e.label: Twelve track
e.description: Twelve track configuration is used in professional recording studios to permit separate control of various tracks which are later mixed to produce a stereophonic or quadraphonic recording.

f.label: Sixteen track
f.description: Sixteen track configuration is used in professional recording studios to permit separate control of various tracks which are later mixed to produce a stereophonic or quadraphonic recording.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Item is not a tape or does not include a tape. For example, code n is used if the item is a disc.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Tape configuration is not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

09.label: Kind of disc, cylinder or tape

a.label: Master tape
a.description:
Final tape production master that is used to make a disc master or a tape duplication master.

Represents the final mix including special processing such as equalization, compression, phasing, and sound synthesis.

b.label: Tape duplication master
b.description:
Sound tape produced from the master tape.

Tape duplication master is played on a tape reproducer to produce the sound tape for cassette, cartridge, or reel.

d.label: Disc master (negative)
d.description:
Negative disc master that is used for the preparation of the mother from which more serviceable and longer lasting metal stampers can be made.

In the early years of recording, discs were pressed from the metal-plated disc master or matrix. As commercial recording developed, the disc master was used, and continues to be used, for the preparation of the mother.

i.label: Instantaneous (recorded on the spot)
i.description: Original recording of a sound event or performance intended for direct reproduction without further processing. In the early years of recording, a single sound event was sometimes recorded simultaneously on several cylinders or discs. All of these recordings would be instantaneous.

m.label: Mass-produced
m.description:
Includes discs or tapes issued as limited pressing or limited issue for private distribution.

Most commercial discs are mass-produced. Mass-produced discs are mechanically pressed for distribution, either commercially or privately; also, tapes reproduced from a tape duplication master for distribution either commercially or privately.

Mass-produced discs, cylinders, and tapes usually include the name of the issuing company, the issue number, and bibliographic information on a printed label or on the container in which the disc, tape, or cylinder is packaged.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Item is not a disc, cylinder, or tape.

r.label: Mother (positive)
r.description:
Exact copy of the original disc recording pressed from the disc master. From the metal mother a negative metal stamper is made to press discs for distribution.

Many stampers may be made from a single mother.

s.label: Stamper (negative)
s.description: Negative metal part, produced from the mother in an electroplating procedure, from which 500 to 750 discs may be pressed.

t.label: Test pressing
t.description: Either one finished disc or one of a very limited pressing is made, designed to be examined aurally before a decision is made to proceed with a pressing.

u.label: Unknown
u.description:
Type of disc, cylinder, or tape is not known.

Also used when it cannot be determined whether the item is instantaneous or mass-produced.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

10.label: Kind of material
10.description: Kind of material used in the manufacture of sound recordings (both instantaneous and mass-produced). This code is only intended to relate to a sound recording rendered on a mechanical device.

a.label: Lacquer coating
a.description: Lacquer coated, but the base material on which the lacquer is applied is not identified. To also identify the base, use codes g (Glass with lacquer), i (Aluminum with lacquer) or r (Paper with lacquer or ferrous oxide).

b.label: Cellulose nitrate
b.description: Cellulose nitrate base. This code may be used for items such as memovox discs.

c.label: Acetate tape with ferrous oxide
c.description: Acetate base with a ferrous oxide coating. May include acetate tape and belts, such as magnabelts.

g.label: Glass with lacquer
g.description: Glass disc base with a lacquer coating.

i.label: Aluminum with lacquer
i.description: Aluminum disc base with a lacquer coating.

l.label: Metal
l.description: Made entirely of metal. Includes the earliest cylinders, which were made of tinfoil, and aluminum transcription discs with no coating, as well as wire and metal tape.

m.label: Plastic with metal
m.description: Made of plastic base with a metal coating. The metal part of such an item is often a thin layer applied to the plastic base. Includes compact audio discs (CDs).

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Kind of material is not applicable to remote digital sound recordings because it pertains to characteristics specific to physical aspects of carriers.

p.label: Plastic
p.description: Made entirely of plastic. Also includes mylar, polyester and vinyl materials. Since the 1950s, commercial or mass-produced sound recordings on 16, 33 1/3, and 45 rpm discs, cassettes, and cartridges are made of plastic.

r.label: Paper with lacquer or ferrous oxide
r.description: Paper or cardboard disc, tape, or cylinder base with a lacquer or ferrous oxide coating.

s.label: Shellac
s.description: Made entirely of shellac. Most commercial or mass-produced 78 rpm discs are made of shellac.

w.label: Wax
w.description: Made entirely of wax. Most instantaneous cylinders were made of wax.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Kind of material used in the manufacture of the item is not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

11.label: Kind of cutting
11.description:
Kind of cutting of the grooves used on a disc.

Primary use is to identify discs which contain only hill-and-dale information.

h.label: Hill-and-dale cutting
h.description:
Vertical cutting, with no lateral information intended for reproduction.

All cylinders and some early discs have this cutting.

l.label: Lateral or combined cutting
l.description: Cutting containing lateral information intended for reproduction. Such discs may also have vertical components intended for reproduction. Most contemporary discs (i.e., all quadraphonic discs and nearly all stereophonic discs) contain both vertical and laterial information and are coded l. Monographic discs are normally lateral only.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description:
Item is not a disc or a cylinder.

Compact audio discs are coded n as they are pitted rather than cut.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Kind of cutting is not known.

12.label: Special playback characteristics
12.description:
Playback characteristics for sound recordings, including special equipment or equalization necessary for proper playback. This code is not used to indicate special processes used during recording unless those processes must be applied during playback.

Codes should be used only if the item in hand includes a clear indication that special playback characteristics are required.

a.label: NAB standard
a.description: National Association of Broadcasters (NAB) standard was used for the transcription of the recording and NAB playback equalization is required.

b.label: CCIR standard
b.description: Comité consultatif de la radiodiffusion (CCIR) standard was used for the transcription of the recording and CCIR playback equalization is required.

c.label: Dolby-B encoded
c.description: Requires Dolby-B decoding playback equipment. Indicated on commercial recordings by the double D insignia (without indication of Dolby-C encoding). If Dolby is used on a tape recording without other indication, Dolby-B may be assumed. Despite the presence of the double-D or "Dolby" on a disc recording, this code is never used for commercial discs.

d.label: dbx encoded
d.description: Used for disc or tape recordings which indicate on the label or package that dbx decoding is required. If descriptive material indicates that dbx was used during recording but that standard playback equipment may be used, this code should not be assigned.

e.label: Digital recording
e.description: Requires digital playback equipment, such as Phillips/Sony Compact Discs or Sony PCM tape recordings. Code e is not used when there is indication that digital equipment was used during recording, but that analog playback equipment may be used. No commercial recordings prior to 1982, and no analog disc or tape recordings require code e.

f.label: Dolby-A encoded
f.description: Requires Dolby-A playback equipment. It is used only for master tapes and other tape recordings where clear indication is given that the professional Dolby-A encoding was applied, and that Dolby-A decoding is required. Dolby-A encoding is never used for commercial tape or discs. (Instantaneous tape recordings labelled "Dolby" without other indication are normally Dolby-B, particularly cassette recordings.)

g.label: Dolby-C encoded
g.description: Requires Dolby-C playback equipment. It is used for tape recordings where the label or packaging clearly indicates that Dolby-C is required. "Dolby" or the double-D symbol without specific explanation normally indicates Dolby-B.

h.label: CX encoded
h.description: Requires CX encoded playback equipment. It is used for recordings where the symbol or mark CX appears. Such recordings may be labelled as compatible with standard playback equipment. No CX recordings will appear with pressing dates prior to 1981.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Item does not have special playback characteristics.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Playback characteristics of the item are not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is applicable.

13.label: Capture and storage technique
13.description: How the sound was originally captured and stored. Re-releases of recordings should be coded for the original capture and storage technique, even though such re-releases may have been enhanced using another technique.

a.label: Acoustical capture, direct storage
a.description: Usually a disc or cylinder recording, captured using an acoustical horn and diaphragm and stored directly on a master surface. Most acoustical recordings date from before 1927/29 when electrical recording equipment became available.

b.label: Direct storage, not acoustical
b.description:
Disc recordings captured using electrical equipment and stored directly on a master surface. All recordings made with microphones and other electrical equipment prior to the availability of magnetic recording techniques in the late 1940s used direct storage.

Commercial recordings marked "direct to disc" or some equivalent phrase also use this technique.

d.label: Digital storage
d.description:
Sound recordings which were captured electrically and stored using digital techniques.

Such recordings are normally identified as "digitally recorded" or some similar phrase on the label or package. "Digital remaster" or "digital mixing" does not imply original digital storage. Note: Digital storage and digital playback should not be confused. The need for digital playback should be recorded in 007/12 (Special playback characteristics).

e.label: Analog electrical storage
e.description: Sound recordings which were captured using electrical techniques and stored as modulations and pulses on a magnetic surface. Most recordings made from the late 1940s until early 1980s are analog electrical recordings.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Capture and storage technique are not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

f.label: Tactile material
f.description: One-character alphabetic code that indicates the category of material to which the item belongs is tactile material. Used for material intended to be read by touch. A fill character (|) is not allowed in this position.

01.label: Specific material designation
01.description: Special class of tactile materialspecific material to which the item belongs.

a.label: Moon
a.description: Tactile material is moon, which is an abstraction of the print.

b.label: Braille
b.description: Tactile material is in braille, which is a system of writing for the blind in which letters, numerals, and punctuation are made of raised dots distinguishable by the fingers.

c.label: Combination
c.description: Item is a combination of two or more of the other defined types.

d.label: Tactile, with no writing system
d.description: Tactile material has no text and is only communicated as graphic, i.e. a raised line diagram or drawing.

u.label: Unspecified
u.description: Special material designation for the tactile material is not specified.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other defined codes is appropriate.

02.label: Undefined
02.description: Contains blank (#) or a fill character (|).

03-04.label: Class of braille writing
03-04.description:
Family of braille to which the item belongs. This is not the particular braille code, but the type of braille code used, representing different types of written symbols. Up to two braille types may be indicated, or the cataloging agency can choose to encode only the predominate type. Multiple codes are coded in order of predominance, if any. If fewer than two codes are assigned, the codes are left justified and unused positions contain blanks (#).

Also coded to identify the class of braille writing used for the text labels of cartographic or graphic items.

.label: No specified class of braille writing
.description: Item consists of fewer than two specified classes of braille writing.

a.label: Literary braille
a.description: Item consists of braille representation for the alphabet, numbers, and punctuation marks commonly used in general writing.

b.label: Format code braille
b.description: Item consists of braille formatting rules for textbooks and related materials.

c.label: Mathematics and scientific braille
c.description: Item consists of braille representations for symbols employed in mathematics and scientific writing.

d.label: Computer braille
d.description: Item consists of braille representations for symbols used in computer programs, texts, and other computer related materials.

e.label: Music braille
e.description: Item consists of braille representations for symbols used in notated music.

m.label: Multiple braille types
m.description: Multiple types and no one type predominates.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Code n in both positions 03-04 indicates that this position is not used because the item is not braille. Code # is also used for braille items in unused positions.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Class of braille writing is not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

05.label: Level of contraction
05.description:
Whether contractions are used.

Contractions are abbreviations consisting of one or more braille or Moon characters to represent common letter combinations.

a.label: Uncontracted
a.description: Includes grade 1 braille.

b.label: Contracted
b.description: Includes Standard English braille, the code for contracted braille of the Braille Authority of the United Kingdom and English Braille, American ed., the code for contracted braille of the Braille Authority of North America.

m.label: Combination
m.description: Item is a combination of contracted and uncontracted.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Item is not braille or Moon.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Level of contraction is not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

06-08.label: Braille music format
06-08.description:
Three-character code that indicates the braille music format of the item. The music formats are the way measures, sections, parts, and related information, such as words, are presented in relation to each other. Up to three formats may be indicated, left justified in order of predominance. If fewer than three codes are assigned, the codes are left justified and unused positions contain blanks (#).

For example, the music format defines how the music for the right and left hand are sequenced and related to each other in braille. Multiple formats are sometimes employed in the same piece of music. For example, a vocal part and text are in one format and the accompaniment is in another.

.label: No specified braille music format
.description: Item uses fewer than three specified braille writing formats.

a.label: Bar over bar
a.description: Measures are displayed in units called parallels and that the beginning of each part’s measure is vertically aligned with the beginning of the same measure for the other part(s). This code is used chiefly for keyboard music.

b.label: Bar by bar
b.description: Music is displayed in indented paragraphs with all of the parts for each measure written consecutively.

c.label: Line over line
c.description: Measures are displayed in parallels, but the measures are not necessarily aligned.

d.label: Paragraph
d.description: Braille music is displayed in paragraphs with one part per paragraph.

e.label: Single line
e.description: Music is presented in segments of two to five lines, the initial line displaying a measure number or rehearsal designation. This code is used for single instrumental parts or solos. It is also called solo instrumental format.

f.label: Section by section
f.description: Hand or part signs are prominent in the left margin.

g.label: Line by line
g.description: Lines of text alternate with lines of music for the preceding text.

h.label: Open score
h.description: Music is presented in parallels. Open score is similar to bar over bar, but used for ensemble scores.

i.label: Spanner short form scoring
i.description: Chord symbols and melody are presented in paragraphs. It is used chiefly for popular and folk music, but music braille is used for the chord symbols. Also used to indicate that the music is in the Canadian melody chord system.

j.label: Short form scoring
j.description: Words, chord symbols, and melody are presented in parallels, and literary braille is used for the chord symbols. It is used chiefly for popular and folk music. This format is also referred to as the American or BANA short form scoring format.

k.label: Outline
k.description: Music is in the outline format.

l.label: Vertical score
l.description: Parts are combined and written as chords.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Code n in all three positions 06-08 indicates that the item is not braille music. Code # is also used for braille music items in unused positions.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Braille music format is not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other defined codes is appropriate.

09.label: Special physical characteristics
09.description: Other special physical characteristics about the braille.

a.label: Print/braille
a.description: Item is eye-readable print with braille interleaved or embossed.

b.label: Jumbo or enlarged braille
b.description: Item is jumbo or enlarged braille, which is used for braille students and braille readers with reduced tactile sensitivity.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Item is not braille.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Special physical characteristics are not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

t.label: Text
t.description: One-character alphabetic code that indicates the category of material to which the item belongs is text, which is defined as printed or manuscript material that is accessible to the naked eye (e.g., a book, a pamphlet, a broadside). A fill character (|) is not allowed in this position.

01.label: Specific material designation
01.description: Special class of textual material to which an item belongs.

a.label: Regular print
a.description: Regular, eye-readable text.

b.label: Large print
b.description: Large print text is oversized print intended for use by the visually impaired.

c.label: Braille
c.description: Braille text is embossed characters that have been formed by raised dots in six-dot cells; braille is intended for use by the visually impaired.

d.label: Loose-leaf
d.description: Text in a loose-leaf binder.

u.label: Unspecified
u.description: Special material designation of the text is not specified.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

z.label: Unspecified
z.description: One-character alphabetic code that indicates the category of material to which the item belongs is unspecified, which means that the item is not identified by one of the other 007 code values or that its multiple physical forms are not being specifically denoted (for instance, when the item in hand is a collection containing different material categories and an institution chooses not to input separate 007 fields for the various components). A fill character (|) is not allowed in this position.

01.label: Specific material designation
01.description: Special class of material to which the item belongs.

m.label: Multiple physical forms
m.description: Multiple physical forms are involved.

u.label: Unspecified
u.description: Physical form of the item is not specified.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

v.label: Videorecording
v.description: One-character alphabetic code that indicates the category of material to which the item belongs is videorecording, which is defined as a recording on which visual images, usually in motion and accompanied by sound, have been registered. It is designed for playback on a television receiver, or video monitor. A fill character (|) is not allowed in this position.

01.label: Specific material designation
01.description: Special class of videorecording to which an item belongs.

c.label: Videocartridge
c.description: Videorecording on tape encased in a cartridge and which has the ends joined together to form a continuous loop.

d.label: Videodisc
d.description: Flat disc of plastic or other material on which video signals, with or without sound, are recorded. Various videodisc systems have been developed (e.g., laser-optical, capacitance, magnetic, etc.).

f.label: Videocassette
f.description: Videorecording on tape encased in a cassette which runs reel-to-reel.

r.label: Videoreel
r.description: Videorecording on a spool of tape mounted on a reel and designed to play from reel-to-reel across a playback pick-up device.

u.label: Unspecified
u.description: Special material designation for the videorecording is not specified.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate.

02.label: Undefined
02.description: Contains blank (#) or a fill character (|).

a.label: One color
a.description: Not used with videorecordings.

b.label: Black-and-white
b.description: Videorecording is executed in black-and-white.

c.label: Multicolored
c.description: Videorecording is executed in more than one color.

m.label: Mixed
m.description: Work or collection is a combination of black-and-white, colored, and/or other images.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Item has no images, e.g., a videorecording with sound only.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: Color characteristics of an item are not known.

z.label: Other
z.description: None of the other codes is appropriate (e.g., videorecording is toned, stained, tinted, etc.).

04.label: Videorecording format
04.description:
Videotape or videodisc recording format.

If a bibliographic record for a videorecording describes various available formats, e.g., Beta and VHS videocassettes, then a separate 007 field is input for each.

a.label: Beta (1/2 in., videocassette)
a.description: Used for the home video system introduced in 1975 by Sony for home videorecording and playback on 1/2 inch videotape. It is distinguished by the size of the cassette, its U-load tape threading, and technical capabilities. This format is also known as Betamax.

b.label: VHS (1/2 in., videocassette)
b.description: Used for the home video system introduced in 1977 by Japan Victor Corporation (JVC) for home videorecording and playback on 1/2 inch videotape. It is distinguished by the size of the cassette, its M-load tape threading, and technical capabilities. VHS stands for "Video Home System."

c.label: U-matic (3/4 in., videocasstte)
c.description: Used for a video format using Sony's trademark name which refers to its tape threading path in a U-shape. It is the worldwide standard for 3/4 inch videotape and is used extensively in industrial and broadcast production. Like the two 1/2 in. home video formats, it uses a helical scan recording system. It is also known as U type standard.

d.label: EIAJ (1/2 in., reel)
d.description: Used for the standard 1/2 inch reel-to-reel helical scan videotape system named for the Electronics Industries Association of Japan which set the standards for 1/2 in. video tape recorders manufactured since 1969. Referred to as "the old trailblazer."

e.label: Type C (1 in., reel)
e.description: Used for the 1 inch videotape recording system utilizing one video head and tape runs at 9.61 inches per second. Type B system uses 2 heads and runs at 9.65 ips; Type A is an obsolete early system. Type B is still used in the U.S. and overseas (as of 1982), but Type C is the 1 inch format most widely employed as the broadcasting standard in the U.S. and overseas. Type C equipment and technology are made by Sony, RCA, and others.
